components.name: Build Primary Button
components.description: Primary action in the default Build lens.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; min-height:2.9rem; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:.68rem 1rem; border:1px solid var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); border-radius:var(--radius-sm, .2rem); background:var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); color:#fff; font-family:var(--font-sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size:.82rem; font-weight:720; cursor:pointer; transition:transform var(--motion-fast, 150ms), background var(--motion-fast, 150ms), color var(--motion-fast, 150ms); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform:translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:translateY(0); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Paper-toned companion action for downloads and adjacent routes.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display:inline-flex; min-height:2.9rem; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:.68rem 1rem; border:1px solid var(--rule-strong, rgba(23,38,36,.34)); border-radius:var(--radius-sm, .2rem); background:rgba(255,255,255,.35); color:var(--ink, #172624); font-family:var(--font-sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size:.82rem; font-weight:720; cursor:pointer; transition:transform var(--motion-fast, 150ms), background var(--motion-fast, 150ms); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { transform:translateY(-2px); background:var(--paper-raised, #fbf8f1); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform:translateY(0); }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: Underlined action used for the assistant and adjacent optional tools.
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { display:inline-flex; min-height:2.9rem; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:.68rem 1rem; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:var(--radius-sm, .2rem); background:transparent; color:var(--ink, #172624); font-family:var(--font-sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size:.82rem; font-weight:720; text-decoration:underline; text-underline-offset:.22em; cursor:pointer; transition:color var(--motion-fast, 150ms), transform var(--motion-fast, 150ms); } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { color:var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); transform:translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; } .ds-btn-quiet:active { transform:translateY(0); }

components.name: Build / Secure Lens Switch
components.description: Explicit two-way content lens; the selected segment is ink-filled and state is announced with aria-pressed.
components.css: .ds-lens-switch { display:inline-flex; padding:.2rem; border:1px solid var(--rule-strong, rgba(23,38,36,.34)); background:rgba(255,255,255,.28); } .ds-lens-option { min-height:2.25rem; padding:.4rem .58rem; border:0; background:transparent; color:var(--muted, #56635f); font-family:var(--font-sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size:.72rem; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer; } .ds-lens-option.is-active { background:var(--ink, #172624); color:var(--paper, #f4f0e6); } .ds-lens-option:hover:not(.is-active) { color:var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); } .ds-lens-option:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Camera Journey Rail
components.description: Seven-stage portfolio orientation with a visible progress path, registered camera poses, and an exposed active label.
components.html:
1. Overview
  2. Selected work
  3. Capabilities
components.css: .ds-journey { width:12rem; color:var(--ink, #172624); } .ds-journey ol { position:relative; display:grid; gap:.18rem; margin:0; padding:.35rem 0; list-style:none; } .ds-journey ol::before { position:absolute; top:1.35rem; bottom:1.35rem; left:1.55rem; width:1px; background:var(--rule-strong, rgba(23,38,36,.34)); content:''; } .ds-journey a { position:relative; display:grid; min-height:3.1rem; grid-template-columns:3.1rem 1fr; align-items:center; border:1px solid transparent; color:var(--muted, #56635f); text-decoration:none; } .ds-journey svg { z-index:1; width:2.35rem; margin:auto; overflow:visible; } .ds-journey svg path { fill:rgba(22,122,114,.08); stroke:currentColor; } .ds-journey svg rect { fill:var(--paper-raised, #fbf8f1); stroke:currentColor; } .ds-journey svg circle { fill:var(--teal, #167a72); stroke:currentColor; } .ds-journey span { font-family:var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size:.61rem; } .ds-journey .is-active a { border-color:var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); background:var(--paper-raised, #fbf8f1); box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(23,38,36,.12); color:var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); } .ds-journey a:hover { color:var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); } .ds-journey a:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Active Filter Chip
components.description: Square evidence filter that communicates state with fill, border, text, and aria-pressed.
components.css: .ds-filter-chip { min-height:2.55rem; padding:.5rem .7rem; border:1px solid var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); background:rgba(22,122,114,.1); color:var(--teal-deep, #0b514c); font-family:var(--font-sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size:.72rem; font-weight:650; cursor:pointer; } .ds-filter-chip span { margin-left:.25rem; font-family:var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size:.58rem; } .ds-filter-chip:hover { background:rgba(22,122,114,.16); } .ds-filter-chip:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; } .ds-filter-chip:active { background:rgba(22,122,114,.22); }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: Square raised-paper field with a small mono label and visible signal focus.
components.css: .ds-field { display:grid; gap:.4rem; max-width:35rem; color:var(--muted, #56635f); font-family:var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size:.67rem; font-weight:600; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-field input { width:100%; min-height:3rem; padding:.65rem .8rem; border:1px solid var(--rule-strong, rgba(23,38,36,.34)); border-radius:0; background:var(--paper-raised, #fbf8f1); color:var(--ink, #172624); font-family:var(--font-sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size:1rem; text-transform:none; } .ds-field input:hover { border-color:var(--ink-soft, #31413e); } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Evidence Cell
components.description: Flat ruled cell for contribution, method, result, or proof context.
components.html:
Technical approach
Discrete simulation, constraint modeling, and decision-ready schedule generation.
components.css: .ds-evidence { margin:0; border:1px solid var(--rule, rgba(23,38,36,.18)); background:var(--rule, rgba(23,38,36,.18)); } .ds-evidence div { padding:.85rem; background:var(--paper, #f4f0e6); } .ds-evidence dt { color:var(--faint, #626e6a); font-family:var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size:.62rem; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-evidence dd { margin:.4rem 0 0; color:var(--ink-soft, #31413e); font-family:var(--font-sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size:.83rem; line-height:1.55; } .ds-evidence:hover { border-color:var(--rule-strong, rgba(23,38,36,.34)); } .ds-evidence:focus-within { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Active Camera Selector
components.description: Selected work, capability, proof, or resume viewpoint with CameraGlyph, title, compact metadata, and aria-selected state.
components.css: .ds-camera-selector { display:grid; width:17rem; min-height:5rem; grid-template-columns:2.8rem 1fr; align-items:center; gap:.1rem .55rem; padding:.65rem .75rem; border:1px solid var(--rule-strong, rgba(23,38,36,.34)); background:var(--ink, #172624); color:var(--paper, #f4f0e6); cursor:pointer; text-align:left; } .ds-camera-selector svg { grid-row:1/3; width:2.5rem; overflow:visible; } .ds-camera-selector svg path:first-child { fill:rgba(244,240,230,.08); stroke:currentColor; } .ds-camera-selector svg rect { fill:var(--paper-raised, #fbf8f1); stroke:currentColor; } .ds-camera-selector svg circle { fill:var(--teal, #167a72); stroke:currentColor; } .ds-camera-selector .ds-axis { fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-dasharray:2 3; opacity:.58; } .ds-camera-selector span { font-family:var(--font-sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size:.72rem; font-weight:720; line-height:1.2; } .ds-camera-selector small { font-family:var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size:.54rem; } .ds-camera-selector:hover { color:#fff; } .ds-camera-selector:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Spatial Field Diagram
components.description: Localization-inspired visual bridge using a pose path, landmarks, uncertainty, and reconstruction geometry.
components.css: .ds-spatial-field { margin:0; border:1px solid var(--rule-strong, rgba(23,38,36,.34)); background:rgba(251,248,241,.65); box-shadow:0 18px 54px rgba(33,43,39,.11); color:var(--muted, #56635f); transition:transform 480ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); } .ds-spatial-field > div { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; padding:.58rem .7rem; border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule, rgba(23,38,36,.18)); font-family:var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size:.56rem; } .ds-spatial-field svg { display:block; width:100%; } .ds-grid { fill:none; stroke:rgba(23,38,36,.08); } .ds-path { fill:none; stroke:var(--ink, #172624); stroke-width:2; } .ds-uncertainty { fill:rgba(22,122,114,.1); stroke:var(--teal, #167a72); stroke-width:1.2; stroke-dasharray:4 3; } .ds-landmarks { fill:var(--teal, #167a72); } .ds-frustum { fill:rgba(116,89,133,.07); stroke:var(--violet, #745985); stroke-width:1.4; } .ds-spatial-field figcaption { padding:.75rem; border-top:1px solid var(--rule, rgba(23,38,36,.18)); font-family:var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size:.64rem; } .ds-spatial-field:hover { transform:translateY(-2px); } .ds-spatial-field:focus-within { outline:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--teal, #167a72) 68%, white); outline-offset:3px; }

narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a code-led survey of one engineering practice from a sequence of deliberately registered viewpoints. It retains the warmth and truthfulness of a laboratory field notebook, but the governing composition is no longer one continuous ledger: Overview, Selected Work, Capabilities, Journey, Proof, Résumés, and Contact are distinct observation fields connected by a visible camera path. Each chapter controls its own paper tint, camera pose, registration label, sparse observations, and active evidence panel. Visual seed `4293f8f6` remains the reproducibility anchor for this world.

The first viewport states Rahul's positioning and explicit actions on the left, localizes that claim through the spatial field on the right, and keeps the camera journey subordinate. Real projects, contributions, distinctions, dates, résumé files, and contact paths remain the primary material. Camera frustums, sparse points, pose paths, reconstruction marks, and uncertainty contours explain how the evidence is observed; they never upgrade an interest or academic foundation into unsupported professional robotics, SLAM, localization, mapping, or Gaussian-splatting delivery.

Build and Secure are semantic lenses over the same world. Build teal or Secure coral owns active state and emphasis, while optimization amber and reconstruction violet keep stable technical meanings. The assistant, Effects Lab, and Spatial World are opt-in depth layers opened from explicit inline hero launchers. Persistent docks are intentionally suppressed so optional tools never obstruct the survey.
keyCharacteristics: Seven registered camera stages connected by a fixed desktop rail or sticky horizontal responsive rail.
Warm laboratory paper, chapter-specific tinted neutrals, dark green-black ink, and sparse technical signals.
Archivo for claims and reading; IBM Plex Mono for frames, coordinates, counts, methods, dates, and state.
One active work, capability, proof, or résumé view at a time, with the complete factual archive still searchable.
CameraGlyph frustums, registration geometry, ruled selectors, and bounded observation panels instead of generic cards.
Restrained one-shot registration motion that is completely removed under reduced-motion preference.

rules.name: The Lens Is a Semantic Switch Rule
rules.body: Build teal and Secure coral may exchange accent ownership; amber and violet keep their technical meanings, and content priority changes without removing evidence.

rules.name: The Registered Field Rule
rules.body: Chapter tints distinguish viewpoints without turning the portfolio into disconnected themes; every tint remains a restrained neutral sheet under the same ink and rule system.

rules.name: The Paper, Not White, Rule
rules.body: Laboratory paper is the default field; pure white is reserved for text on deep filled actions.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Archivo makes claims and carries reading; IBM Plex Mono registers the evidence. Never set long explanatory paragraphs in mono.

rules.name: The Registered View Rule
rules.body: Work, capability, proof, and résumé chapters show one active observation at a time; adjacent evidence belongs in an explicit selector, bounded archive, or search surface.

rules.name: The Journey Is Orientation Rule
rules.body: The camera rail explains position and progress. It stays visually subordinate to the hero claim and chapter evidence, never becoming game HUD chrome.

rules.name: The 320px Integrity Rule
rules.body: At the narrowest supported width, preserve the claim, active camera label, primary action, résumé path, assistant path, and optional-world links without overlap or horizontal scrolling.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Resting evidence uses tint, rules, clipping, and registration geometry; elevation appears only for localization, sticky state, active journey position, or a modal layer.

rules.name: The Camera Must Observe Rule
rules.body: A camera glyph or frustum must identify a viewpoint, active selector, stage, or spatial relationship; never use it as an ornamental tech icon.

rules.name: The Signal Geometry Rule
rules.body: Curves and circles describe a person, observation, trajectory, uncertainty, or state; the editorial container system stays predominantly square.

rules.name: The Optional Worlds Rule
rules.body: Assistant, effects, and Three.js experiences may deepen the portfolio, but no recruiter-critical fact, proof, résumé, or contact action may exist only inside them.

dos: Do lead with the positioning claim, explicit actions, and real evidence before optional spectacle.
Do preserve the seven-stage story: position → selected system → capabilities → journey → proof → targeted résumé → contact.
Do use chapter tints, CameraGlyph poses, sparse observations, and frame labels to distinguish registered viewpoints.
Do keep one active work, capability, proof, or résumé panel visible while preserving searchable archives and clearly labeled selectors.
Do keep Journey concise at four default entries and keep Share Bench collapsed until requested.
Do use inline hero launchers for the assistant, Effects Lab, and Spatial World while persistent docks remain suppressed.
Do preserve visible focus, semantic headings and landmarks, active-label exposure on mobile, 2.75rem coarse-pointer targets, readable contrast, and meaningful alt text.
Do remove registration, panel, camera, progress, spatial, and decorative motion under reduced-motion preference.
donts: Don't collapse the chapters back into one long ledger or an equal-weight wall of cards.
Don't turn the camera journey into a dominant game HUD, sticky obstruction, or unlabeled row of mystery icons.
Don't use chapter tints as unrelated themes; they are calibrated neutrals inside one paper-and-ink world.
Don't turn robotics, localization, mapping, probabilistic reasoning, reconstruction, or Gaussian-splatting motifs into unsupported experience claims.
Don't replace the world with generic AI gradients, neon cyber styling, SaaS chrome, stock robots, or copied reference-site imagery and shapes.
Don't use IBM Plex Mono for long reading copy or let decorative numbering crowd essential mobile content.
Don't let animation, pointer precision, optional tools, or heavy rendering block the default reading and action path.
